passage:
Rain hammered the bus shelter, and there was no dustbin in sight. Santosh, ten, finished his biscuit and crumpled the wrapper. A man beside him had just dropped a cup onto the road. "Everyone does it," Santosh muttered, and raised his arm to toss.
His father Eshaan calmly folded his own wrapper and slipped it into his shirt pocket. He said nothing.
Santosh saw. He held the wrapper for a moment, then pushed it into his own pocket. At home they found the bin, and Eshaan dropped his in first.

qa.q: What did Eshaan do with his own wrapper?
qa.a: Eshaan folded it and slipped it into his shirt pocket.

qa.q: How did Santosh feel when he muttered 'Everyone does it', and why?
qa.a: Santosh felt comfortable tossing the wrapper, even justified, because there was no dustbin and a man beside him had just dropped a cup.

qa.q: What turning point made Santosh keep his wrapper?
qa.a: Santosh saw his father quietly pocket his own wrapper without a lecture, so he copied that instead.

qa.q: What might Eshaan have been hoping when he pocketed the wrapper and said nothing?
qa.a: Eshaan may have hoped that showing was better than telling, and that Santosh would follow the example.

grounding: A child throws a wrapper because grown-ups do, and a parent who pockets the trash teaches more than a lecture.

passage:
Lavanya, nine, watched an auto driver toss a chips packet out of his window at the colony gate. The next day, after her ice cream, she dropped the stick and wrapper beside the gate, too. Her father Mohit said nothing. He bent, picked them up, and walked the twenty steps to the bin near the security cabin.
"Why did you take mine?" asked Lavanya.
"The bin is there for all of us," Mohit said. "I didn't want the gate to look dirty for the neighbours."
The next evening, holding her wrapper, Lavanya looked at the gate, then at the bin. She walked all the way over and dropped it in herself. Mohit was reading the newspaper, but his mouth twitched.

qa.q: How many steps did Mohit walk to the bin?
qa.a: Mohit walked twenty steps to the bin near the security cabin.

qa.q: What was Lavanya thinking when she dropped her ice cream stick and wrapper beside the gate?
qa.a: She was copying what she had seen the auto driver do, and felt it did not matter.

qa.q: What choice did Lavanya make the next evening, and what led to it?
qa.a: She walked to the bin and dropped her wrapper in herself, after her father quietly picked up hers and explained the bin is for everyone.

qa.q: How might Mohit have felt seeing Lavanya use the bin?
qa.a: Mohit was probably quietly pleased, since his mouth twitched though he kept reading the newspaper.

grounding: A child drops a wrapper because grown-ups do, and a parent who picks up litter teaches more than a lecture.
